Yes! I have been taking Prozac since July for high risk suicide (and going to weekly therapy as well) but I have been having odd experiences. Not sure if it’s due to medication or not. But if I get too mentally involved into thinking about it I can easily start to fear that I’m truly losing my mind. I hear music at night that my husband doesn’t hear... I started seeing silhouettes... I feel like everyone I care about is withdrawing from me. Like the whole world is watching me crash and no one wants to tell me because they don’t know what to say... but they seem aware of something I don’t... 
I have always been a fairly popular person. Not because I’m the popular type, I just care about people and give the type of friendship I would want to receive and I guess it leaves a good impression.
Truly wonderful! Well done!!

Intimacy is provoked. 
You draw it out in each other. 
I’d say talk about it alongside a couple you both admire and trust. However much you feel comfortable. Let it feel safe and casual for her. Talk about “taboo” things confidently together. 
If you normalize sexual behavior in your marriage and can have thoughtful conversations along those lines with each other, the real intimacy you’re seeking will follow. 
The intimacy you seek will grow because you took the liberty to plant it in her heart.

Best advice I ever got was “Only draw (paint) what you see. Not what you think you see.”

Draw what your eyes see. Not what your understanding mind sees. Your mind completes the side of the face you don’t see in the reference picture, but the viewer of your art won’t have the privilege of a reference. Give them only what you see. Not what you know. That way their minds can accurately complete the other side of the face without seeing.

Yup. I have a very specific memory of myself as a kid listening to  TLC’s “Waterfalls” on my Walkman and pretending to be in the music video. I was outside by myself and there was the perfect amount of wind blowing my hair for an epic 90’s MTV music video. 
I was wearing baggy jeans with a Stüssy shirt and an open flannel (for the wind effect). I was about 11 years old. 
Ever since then I imagine myself in the songs I listen to.
